=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- File: scripts/claude_issue_route.py
  Location: has_trusted_reclarify, line ~266, `body.startswith(RECLARIFY_COMMAND_PREFIX)`
  Issue: The `/reclarify` gate uses bare `startswith("/reclarify")`, so `/reclarifyXYZ`, `/reclarify-bypass`, and similar prefixes would be accepted as a vouching comment. The test `[_comment(body="/reclarify please", association="MEMBER")]` is intentionally matched, but the boundary is broader than the literal command name in the plan ("commented `/reclarify`).
  Suggested minimal fix: tighten to `body == "/reclarify" or body.startswith("/reclarify\n") or body.startswith("/reclarify ")`. Update one test row (`"/reclarify please"`).
  Estimated lines changed: 2

- File: scripts/claude_issue_intake.sh
  Location: `if ! [[ "${dispatcher_login}" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9-]*(\[bot\])?$ ]]; then`, ~line 156
  Issue: The login regex accepts trailing hyphens (e.g. `user-`), which GitHub itself rejects. Not a security bypass because the permission read still fails on an invalid login, but the guard's contract drifts from GitHub's documented login rules.
  Suggested minimal fix: `^[A-Za-z0-9]([A-Za-z0-9-]*[A-Za-z0-9])?(\[bot\])?$`.
  Estimated lines changed: 1

- File: scripts/claude_issue_intake.sh
  Location: reject() at the `dispatcher_not_authorized` branch, line ~197
  Issue: The `dispatcher(s) $(jq -c '.' "${PERMISSIONS_FILE}")` detail includes the full permissions map in the Telegram ERROR. Acceptable for operators, but the detail could be tightened to the offending login only.
  Suggested minimal fix: when reason is `dispatcher_not_authorized`, log only the failing login (already known in scope). One-line jq change.
  Estimated lines changed: 3
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
- File: scripts/claude_issue_intake.sh
  Location: lines 166-167, 174-175, 192-194 (reject detail for authorization_read_failed)
  Issue: The reject() detail for authorization_read_failed reads the first 200 bytes of the error file, but gh_retry_to_file internally captures the command's stderr in a private temp file and only emits its own ::warning:: lines to the caller's stderr redirect. The operator sees "gh command failed (attempt 1/5)..." rather than the actual API error (e.g., "HTTP 404" or "Resource not accessible").
  Suggested minimal fix: After a failed gh_retry_to_file call, the actual last-attempt error is already gone (temp file deleted). Instead, grep for the "::error::" line that gh_retry_to_file emits on final failure, which includes the command: `detail="$(grep '::error::' "${RUNTIME_DIR}/permission_error.txt" | head -1)"`. Alternatively, accept the current diagnostic — it already names the failing command and attempt count.
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
